physicalNotes: Radius 0.20786903 Jupiter radii from Poultourtzidis et al. 2026 (2026A&A...707A.106P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.106P/abstract): 14,861 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.02422691 Jupiter masses (Poultourtzidis et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026A&A...707A.106P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.106P/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Poultourtzidis et al. 2026 (2026A&A...707A.106P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname POULTOURTZIDIS_ET_AL_2026): P 4.6594779 d
sources.shape: Poultourtzidis et al. 2026 (2026A&A...707A.106P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname POULTOURTZIDIS_ET_AL_2026): a/R* 25.5; Poultourtzidis et al. 2026 (2026A&A...707A.106P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname POULTOURTZIDIS_ET_AL_2026): inclination 88.24 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Poultourtzidis et al. 2026 (2026A&A...707A.106P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname POULTOURTZIDIS_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2459369.83103 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 2 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
